records.position_on: the Rescissions Act of 2025 (H.R. 4), a partisan package rescinding enacted funding for public broadcasting and foreign aid
records.confidence_reason: She urges a no vote on the rescissions package in two floor speeches on consecutive days and says it should be rejected outright; held at 0.75 because she says she is open to targeted rescissions in a bipartisan spending bill, so part of her objection is to the partisan process rather than to cutting spending as such.

sources.excerpt: "Saving a couple pennies is not worth losing our credibility or causing millions of deaths across the globe." ... "And if my colleagues agree, which I believe many of you do, then the course we must take is clear. We have to reject this package outright." ... "I urge my colleagues to protect that trust, and join me in voting no."
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-28. Her Senate floor remarks as published by the Appropriations Committee minority office she leads as Vice Chair. Date from the page.

sources.excerpt: "We have never, never before seen bipartisan investments, slashed through a partisan rescissions package. Do not start now." ... "I urge my colleagues to join me in voting NO."
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-28. Her floor remarks the next day, ahead of final passage, from the same office. Same package; not independent of the first source.

records.position_on: the REINS Act (H.R. 427, 2015), which would require congressional approval of every major agency rule
records.confidence_reason: He says in his own statement that he strongly opposes the REINS Act because it would block agency rules that protect the environment; one source from 2015, so held at 0.8.

This bill is a blatant attempt by House Republicans to create another hurdle for the Administration to protect the environment and to act boldly on a foremost issue of our time – combating climate change."
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-28. His statement on his official House site. Date from the page.
